Follow See All Science The Apple Watch Series 12 is the start of a new wearable era A surprisingly consequential update for the world’s most popular smartwatch.

With the latter, Apple is potentially kicking the door down on what’s been a niche, nascent, and recently problematic market. (Either way you slice it, AI is part of the equation.) Most of the ideas explored with the Series 12 aren’t novel, but they haven’t been implemented by a company with Apple’s scale or reputation.

8 Verge Score Apple Watch Series 12 $ 399 $ 399 The Good Faster charging Redesigned sensor array Ceramic is back Thoughtful privacy structure for Audio Intelligence Siri on the wrist is more useful The Bad Thoughtful privacy may not change how laypeople feel Many of the new features aren’t available at launch $399 at Amazon $399 at Apple $399 at Best Buy How we rate and review products After a week with the Series 12, I can’t say I have a complete picture.
Several of the most interesting health and AI features aren’t launching until later this year and weren’t available for review.
This is a significant hardware redesign compared to previous Apple Watches.

Together, these hardware upgrades enable a host of new software features, including more frequent heart rate sampling, a new readiness score, and a brave new world of Audio Intelligence, which is what Apple is calling its upcoming suite of AI-powered ambient listening features.
Most notably, the redesigned sensors mean the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are now capable of truly continuous heart rate monitoring.
Siri AI is more front and center in watchOS 27.

Apple put out a white paper comparing how accurate its continuous heart rate monitoring is to a gold-standard Polar H10 chest strap, as well as competitors like the Pixel Watch 4, Samsung Galaxy Watch 8, Oura Ring 5, and Whoop across several types of workouts and at rest. (It’s an interesting read for wearable nerds!) I’d need roughly eight arms and legs to replicate this study in a week, and alas, I’m not an octopus.
However, I did wear an H10 chest strap during two runs (one steady state and one interval run), a walk, and while at rest.
Judging solely on what’s available today, this is a straightforward hardware upgrade that closes the gap between Apple and the standout perks of more niche rivals like Whoop and Oura.
For those pondering upgrades, Apple has laid a strong foundation with its hardware for some ambitious features down the road.

I’d understand if you have qualms about Audio Intelligence and privacy, and to those folks: I’ll remind you that last year’s models are still great, probably available on sale, and don’t come with as many privacy questions.
